transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

It is unlikely to be the heating element just yet. In most Samsung washer-dryers like yours, damp clothes after a cycle are caused by restricted airflow (a blocked lint filter or condenser) or simply overloading the drum for drying purposes. Please check if the load was within the specified dry capacity (typically 5kg for an 8-9kg machine) and ensure the lint filter and condenser are clean. If these are clear and the load was appropriate, we can then look at whether the heater is actually producing heat.
I load a full 9kg drum and wash and dry in one go. The manual says 6kg dry capacity for drying, so I guess that's over. The drum does get hot during drying though, and I get no error codes.

[Heading: Overloading the drum for drying]
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The issue is simply that you are putting a 9kg wet load into a machine with a 6kg drying capacity. A washer-dryer can only remove moisture from about half the weight it washes because there isn't enough air circulation to dry a full load effectively, even if the heat is on. To fix this, split your laundry: wash the full 9kg load, but then only put up to 6kg (roughly two-thirds of the drum) into the drying cycle. You will need to run the second batch separately. If you continue to dry full loads, the clothes will always come out damp.

candidates.cause: Restricted airflow (blocked lint filter or condenser)
Faulty drying heater element or thermal cut-out
